name: MANS (Multi-byte ANS compressor)
baseline: FSE-ANS (Finite State Entropy) on CPU; nvCOMP Huffman on GPU; 16-bit Huffman for ratio
workload: Compression and decompression of multi-byte (16/32-bit) integer scientific data; CPU run on an Intel Xeon Gold 5220S, GPU runs on NVIDIA A100 and AMD MI210; Adaptive Data Mapping converts multi-byte integers to 8-bit symbols before ANS.
claimed_speedup: CPU: 1.92x faster compression and 2.04x faster decompression vs FSE-ANS; 1.24x higher compression ratio than FSE-ANS in portable mode (README also lists 2.37x vs FSE-ANS in ratio mode). A100: 45.14x faster compression vs nvCOMP Huffman.
hardware: Intel Xeon Gold 5220S CPU; NVIDIA A100 GPU; AMD MI210 GPU
tradeoffs: Targets multi-byte integer data (HPC and sensor slices), not generic byte streams. Needs OpenMP; GPU paths need CUDA 12.6 or ROCm. The portable CPU mode trades some ratio for consistency with the GPU format.
caveats: README numbers only: the figure images (THR.png, CR.png) carry the detail, no compiler flags or benchmark scripts were checked, and the per-dataset speedups are averages. A peer-reviewed SC25 paper (doi 10.1145/3712285.3759825) exists but ACM is blocked here, so it was not opened; a verifier with ACM access could raise the tier to B. The README's two ratio figures vs FSE-ANS (2.37x and 1.24x) differ by mode and are listed inconsistently in places. The 288x and 135x figures compare GPU to the project's own CPU mode, not to a third-party baseline.
found_via: WebSearch 'MANS ANS encoding multi-byte integer data CPUs GPUs github code repository' (surfaced from a search for ANS libraries), then README on raw.githubusercontent.com

name: Turbo-Histogram (TurboHist)
baseline: Naive single-table byte histogram loop (hist_1_8), plus Ryg's histogram variants and Countbench; the histogram is the counting stage of Huffman, FSE and rANS encoders
workload: Byte-frequency histogram construction over 1 GB inputs (enwik9 text, enwik9 after BWT, and all zeros), single thread, large-file benchmark rather than cache-resident.
claimed_speedup: Up to 22 times faster than the naive solution (README headline). Table: on enwik9 hist_8_64 4053.37 MB/s (0.9035 cycles/byte) vs naive hist_1_8 2761.01 MB/s (1.3423); on enwik9.bwt histr_8_64 5135.29 MB/s (0.7229) vs naive 1170.89 MB/s (3.0642); all-zeros histr_8_64 reaches 19629.28 MB/s vs naive 877.27 MB/s.
compiler_and_flags: gcc 11.2; flags not stated in README (built via the repo makefile)
tradeoffs: C with a C++-compatible header, no inline assembly in the main functions (an optional inline-asm variant is also provided). Counts bytes only; it is a building block for entropy coders, not a coder itself.
caveats: Off-center for the category: it speeds up the histogram stage of an entropy coder, and the 'naive' baseline is the project's own scalar loop, so the headline 22x is on skewed or constant data where the naive loop stalls on store-to-load dependencies. On ordinary text the gain over naive is about 1.5x (derived from page data: 4053 vs 2761 MB/s). Flags not stated; README is first-party. Its fastest listed row is an inline-asm variant (hist_8_64asm 4161.87 MB/s) and Ryg asm variants reach 4132.54 MB/s, so the portable C win over the best third-party asm is small. License file is the two-clause BSD text without an SPDX header; the SPDX id is inferred from the text.
found_via: WebSearch 'fast histogram byte frequency counting for entropy coding github C++ SIMD' ; opened README and LICENSE via raw.githubusercontent.com

name: DietGPU (GPU rANS codec)
baseline: nvCOMP ANS (NVIDIA proprietary GPU ANS codec); the README itself compares against nothing
workload: Batched GPU rANS encode and decode of byte arrays on an A100 (README) and on an H100 (third-party paper snippet), 4 KiB segments per warp, 9-11 bit probability precision.
claimed_speedup: README: ANS codec 'operates at throughputs around 250-410 GB/s for reasonable data sizes on an A100 GPU'. Third-party snippet (arXiv 2606.18900, not opened): 592.5 GB/s decode and 364.9 GB/s encode on H100, above the 480 GB/s the snippet attributes to nvcomp-ANS.
tradeoffs: CUDA only, needs inputs of roughly 512 KiB or more to amortise overhead; per-array statistics; byte-wise symbols only; probability precision limited to 9, 10 or 11 bits. Python/PyTorch API plus a C++ raw-pointer API.
caveats: The README reports absolute throughput with no head-to-head baseline, so the 'faster than nvCOMP ANS' claim rests on a search-result snippet of a paper that could not be opened (arXiv blocked), and nvCOMP ANS is proprietary. Repository was archived by the owner on 2026-06-14 (read-only). Benchmarks use torch.normal-derived data, not real corpora. Tier D would apply if the paper claim is discounted; a verifier with arXiv access should open 2606.18900.
found_via: WebSearch 'nvCOMP ANS alternative open source GPU rANS compressor github faster than nvcomp ANS throughput GB/s'; README read via raw.githubusercontent.com; commit date via github.com/facebookresearch/dietgpu/commits
